title: Free Will & Determinism
rootClaim: Human beings possess genuine free will, exerting conscious agency and moral responsibility over their choices.

branches.text: First-person subjective experience provides direct, intuitive evidence of conscious deliberation and choice.

children.text: Agent-Causation: Conscious minds act as uncaused initiators of events, distinct from deterministic event-event physical chains.
Violates Physical Closure: Agent-causation relies on non-physical mind-matter interactions that violate energy conservation without explaining how non-physical minds intervene.

Introspective Illusion: Introspection is unobservable and unreliable; psychological research demonstrates humans routinely construct post-hoc rationalizations for choices determined by unconscious drivers.
Moral & Legal Systems: Society logically requires personal agency, praise, and blame for intentional actions.
Consequentialist Pragmatism: Legal systems function as social tools for deterrence and incentive structuring, requiring predictable causal responsibility rather than metaphysical agency.
Retributive Justice: Legal institutions and contractual accountability presuppose genuine moral responsibility rather than puppet causation.
Quarantine Model of Justice: Society can justify detaining dangerous individuals to protect public safety (like medical quarantine) without invoking retributive moral blame.

branches.text: Neuroscience indicates that decisions are formulated by pre-conscious neural processes prior to subjective awareness.

children.text: Deliberative Complexity Gap: Laboratory experiments measure arbitrary rapid motor movements, which fail to generalize to reflective, long-term decisions involving moral reasoning.
Libet Experiments: Motor readiness potentials in the brain build up hundreds of milliseconds before an agent reports conscious intent.
Stochastic Accumulation Model: Modern neuroimaging suggests readiness potentials reflect random background neural noise crossing an activation threshold rather than a committed decision.
Epiphenomenal Consciousness: Conscious awareness is a passive observer of neural activity rather than the executive controller.
Evolutionary Expense Paradox: High metabolic costs of conscious brain processing would be evolutionary impossibilities if awareness conferred zero survival or behavioral advantage.
Veto Power ('Free Won't'): Conscious awareness retains executive power to consciously veto pre-conscious impulses before physical execution.
Pre-conscious Veto Initiation: The decision to veto an impulse is itself preceded by unconscious neural processing, shifting determinism back one step.

branches.text: Compatibilism: Free will is compatible with physical determinism when defined as acting on internal desires without external coercion.

children.text: Manipulation Argument: If an agent is covertly engineered by neuroscientists to desire X, they satisfy compatibilist freedom while remaining completely controlled, demonstrating compatibilism is insufficient for true responsibility.
Second-Order Volition: Freedom consists of reflective alignment between higher-order desires and immediate motivations.
Infinite Regress of Desires: Higher-order desires are themselves subject to prior physical or psychological causes; adding layers of reflection does not escape deterministic causation.

branches.text: Hard Determinism: Every physical event, including human brain states, is completely determined by preceding physical causes and natural laws.

children.text: Quantum Indeterminism: Fundamental physics via quantum mechanics shows that physical nature at the microscopic scale is probabilistic rather than strictly deterministic.
The Luck Problem: If actions are uncaused or quantum-random, they represent stochastic chance rather than intentional free choice.

Adequate Determinism & Emergence: Macroscopic brain processes integrate quantum randomness into structured probabilistic choices, allowing indeterminism to yield options without making choices arbitrary.

definitions.description: The capacity of a rational being to make moral judgments and be held morally accountable for actions.
The philosophical view that causal determinism and free will are logically compatible perspectives.
The view that causal determinism is true and completely rules out free will and moral responsibility.
The capacity of conscious awareness to inhibit or veto motor actions initiated by pre-conscious brain processes.
The cognitive bias in which humans falsely believe they have direct insight into the origins of their mental states.
A philosophical thought experiment asserting that if covert neuro-manipulation undermines free will, determinism must do so as well under identical conditions.
A neuroscientific framework proposing that readiness potentials represent random fluctuations of neural noise reaching a decision threshold rather than pre-conscious intent.
A consequentialist penal framework that justifies detaining dangerous individuals for public safety, analogous to medical quarantine, without requiring moral retributivism.
The principle in physics asserting that every physical event has a sufficient physical cause, leaving no room for non-physical mental intervention.
